7.text: PSYCHOLOGY OF THE SHAMANS. — I have already said that most of the

8.text: Chukchee shamans are very nervous, highly excitable persons, often almost

9.text: on the verge of insanity. To make this statement clearer, I will try to give

10.text: instances of this in more detail.

11.text: A shaman from the Telkäˊp tundra, by name Keleˊwg̣i (“Keˊlᴇ-man”), with

12.text: whom I made acquaintance in the Mariinsky Post, had, even among the

13.text: Russians, the reputation of an odd customer, of one who seeks a quarrel on the

14.text: slightest provocation. Once he came to a Russian cossack, bringing a couple

15.text: of half hairless reindeer-skins, and peremptorily demanded to be paid for them

16.text: a price quite out of proportion to the real value of even the best skins of

17.text: that kind. On the refusal of the cossack, he instantly drew his knife, in-

18.text: tending to strike, but happily the cossack turned aside the blow with a stick.

19.text: Immediately afterwards the too exacting trader was turned out of the barracks

20.text: where this incident had taken place.

21.text: Shortly after my arrival, Keleˊwg̣i came to me and declared his intention

22.text: of giving me valuable material in relation to the abode of “spirits” and their

23.text: ways with men. His accounts, however, were too incoherent and contradic-

24.text: tory to be of any great value. Among other things, he gave me his biog-

25.text: raphy. He was a grandson of a great shaman, Tɪluˊu, long since deceased.

26.text: When he was still quite a young lad, a voice said to him, “Go into the

27.text: wilderness: there you will find a tiny drum. Try it and prove its qualities.”

28.text: He found the drum and began to exercise on it. Then he saw all the

29.text: world, — both shores of the Anadyr River and the whole tundra. After

30.text: that, he ascended to the sky and pitched his tent on the ground of the clouds.

31.text: From that time on, he took to the practice of shamanism. Soon he equalled

32.text: his grandfather in power, and then surpassed him.

33.text: All this was evidently borrowed from various tales and incantations.

34.text: For instance, a tiny drum made of the skin of a beetle, or even of a small

35.text: louse, figures in several stories, Chukchee and Koryak. When found in the

36.text: wilderness, and shown to be of a supernatural kind, it gives to its possessor

37.text: immense shamanistic power.¹ The same may also be said about the ground

40.text: and of the corresponding high pay he should receive for it, that he brought

41.text: to the fair nothing but this treasure of his mind. For all the provisions and
